growth_signal.value: Series B raised for US expansion; on VivaTech's list, which requires €5M+ yearly revenue and 40% growth for three years

raised.value: $67M over three rounds, including a $45M Series B in February 2026

entry.idea: Software that reads the piles of documents brokers send to specialty insurers, sorts the risks and lets underwriters price and bind them in a fraction of the time.
entry.lesson: Pick the corner of a giant industry that still runs on email, and build the boring plumbing the incumbents will never build themselves.
entry.name: Artificial

growth.basis: substitute: curated list criteria and funding round
growth.reason: Qualified for a list requiring 40% yearly growth, but no numbers of its own published.

market.reason: Specialty and commercial insurance moves hundreds of billions a year, but the buyers are a limited set of insurers and brokers.

tech.reason: Deep domain software built over a decade with insurers; not novel science, but slow for a newcomer to match.

entry.twist: It targets the Lloyd's of London market, where huge, unusual risks are still placed by email and PDF, and lets several insurers underwrite together through one algorithm.
entry.who_pays: Insurers and brokers such as Apollo, Aon, Convex and Chaucer pay for the platform.
entry.why_now: Language models can finally read messy broker submissions, and specialty insurers are under pressure to cut costs.
